## Summary

The tweet: re-reading his own handbook, two observations — (1) it's "by far the best place for a brand new systematic trader to start" and worth an occasional review; (2) he wants to write **a second edition, updated** — but instead of writing and "getting Claude to tidy it up", he'll **voice-dictate the whole thing**, publishing the full "raw" version the same way he does his Substack articles. "Perhaps a 2027 job..."

The quoted launch tweet (Jun 16) is where the substance sits: the handbook went live free on his website — **24 chapters, start to finish: what an edge actually is, building in MT5, backtesting without fooling yourself, the overfitting trap, position sizing and the maths of ruin, then going live and managing capacity.** Plus a free resources page carrying **the MQL5 order-splitting code he runs live in XAQP** ("cuts market impact and lifts a strategy's capacity ceiling"). Written as "the thing I wish someone had handed me when I switched from discretionary to systematic."

Cover OCR: "THE HANDBOOK ENTRIES LIVE TODAY — FREE TO READ, NO GATE — 24 CHAPTERS — SYSTEMATIC TRADING · SIZING · FILTERS — START TO FINISH … kieranduff.com/handbook". Verified live at capture: https://kieranduff.com/handbook (page title "The Beginner's Guide to Systematic Trading"; overfitting, position sizing, maths-of-ruin and order-splitting sections all present on the page).
